merged.title: fix(rac1/pal): triage overlay assembly from its own directory
merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
## Problem

`games/rac1/tools/triage.py` only looked in the executable's `asm/nonmatchings` directories. Unmatched level functions consequently appeared blocked by missing assembly even when their assembly was present under `asm/overlays`.

## Change

- Recognize level symbols with the existing `rank_candidates.OVERLAY_NAME` pattern and use its `OVERLAY_ASM` directory.
- Classify those bodies as game text, as `rank_candidates.check_names` already does.
- Preserve executable routing, genuine blocker classification and missing-assembly checks.
- Add five asset-free regression tests for shared/level overlays, missing overlay assembly, game text and core text.

With the PAL snapshot from #71 and locally supplied assembly, this fixes 14 false missing-assembly reports: 12 entries return to the work queue, while two remain correctly blocked as handwritten assembly. The counts depend on that source snapshot; some entries are joined fragments rather than independent C functions.

merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
- Android minimum lowered from 10 (API 29) to 9 (API 28): minSdk, the android-arm64 preset and Embree's Android build.

merged.author: Lynder063

Gets the port ready for a VR mod, without adding one. A native mod can now show the game in a headset; the mod owns OpenXR, and the port links no VR library.

The motivation is a future port of the Ratchet & Clank VR mod by [npiriou](https://github.com/npiriou) ([Rerac-vr](https://github.com/npiriou/Rerac-vr), made for ReRAC), which we have permission to bring to OpenRAC. No code of it is in this PR.

## What a mod gets (interface 1.4, SDK 1.4.0)

opened.title: feat(mods): add reusable map packs and native map sessions
opened.author: llesieur99
opened.untrustedBody:
Adds the reusable tools for a creator to export an edited Godot world as a named map mod and launch it in OpenRAC. This patch contains the framework, documentation and synthetic tests; it includes no authored game map or disc-derived assets.

The exporter `editor/map_mod.py` combines a project's terrain and the selected level's packed gameplay/collision files into a format-3 map pack. Older tools reject this format. The launcher installs map packs through Mods, identifies them as maps and passes `--map` so an incompatible executable refuses the session. Stacking enforces one active map and the correct disc version.

The native startup reads the map's name, template level, spawn, heading and scene settings. It starts a fresh session, disables campaign memory cards and sets the class-0 placement before the game's hero/camera initialization. merged.title: Match scalar min/max in C with pinned PS2DEV GCC 3.2.3
merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
Reconstructs `func_001F9B90` (`max_float`) and `func_001F9B98` (`min_float`) as ordinary C comparisons, exactly 8 bytes each. GCC 2.95 adds a register copy; the published PS2DEV GCC 3.2.3 frontend emits the required scalar operations and preserves the existing `FastAbsF` and `IntToFloat` bodies.

The entire `fastfunc.c` object uses an explicit compiler profile with file-wide `-ffast-math`. Setup pins and verifies the GNU release and published PS2DEV patch. The original assembler/linker pipeline remains unchanged. This change introduces no custom compiler patches, instruction edits, register bindings, inline-assembly wrappers, or HLE. It is a reconstruction toolchain, not a claim about retail's original compiler.

merged.title: core: sceCdInit (func_001211B0) without the register pin
merged.author: xx255q
merged.untrustedBody:
Removes the register pin (`register int m __asm__("$4")`) from `sce_cd_init` (func_001211B0, sceCdInit) in `src/core/001208E8.c`.

Retail keeps the shared `-1` in `$a0`; without the pin, local-alloc put it in `$v1`. Passing `cd_scmd_sync`'s non-blocking argument through a local (`int no_wait = 1;`) changes the allocation order so the `-1` lands in `$a0` again, with no pin, inline asm or barrier.

- Same object code as the pinned version (function bytes and relocations compared).
- The permuter result it was reduced from is `tools/try_func.py` EXACT against retail.
- Passes `tools/integrate.py`'s banned-construct check.

Found with decomp-permuter (passes that write empty blocks, dummy arithmetic and the like disabled), then reduced by hand to the one change that matters.

# Match 780 functions, with compiler and assembler fixes measured against retail

This adds C for 777 v1.01 functions and three release-specific ones, plus the
compiler and assembler changes that got them there. Most of it is large level code:
166 of the functions are over 1 KB, and the biggest are the per-level hero state
handlers (30 to 37 KB each).

It is rebased onto master after #329, #331 and #332. 55 functions were matched both
here and in those PRs, mostly #329's `-rc2.c` units. Master's versions stay. Ours are
gone: their units, flags lines and marker edits are removed, and the batch commits that
carried them were renumbered. One commit had only such duplicates and was dropped.
Each of master's 55 still passes `tools/check.py` under this branch's compiler
defaults in all three releases (see Verification).

## What is matched

| Area | Functions | Bytes | Notes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Boot: `src/core/` | 39 | | |
| Boot: `src/game/` | 212 | | |
| Boot, total | 251 | 128

- Where a function only exists in one release, it is demoted with `tools/carry.py --demote` and gets its own copy under `src/pal/` or `src/us2/`.

opened.title: feat(src): mark six DMA wait loops ASM_FUNC
opened.author: DrLegitamate
opened.untrustedBody:
## What

Six 40-byte boot bodies in `src/game/002EEB00.c` marked `ASM_FUNC`: `func_002F1E60`, `func_002F29E4`, `func_002F2A0C`, `func_002F32AC`, `func_002F32D4`, `func_002F4F78`. Each is the same wait loop on a hardware channel register (`-0x3000` or `-0x2C00` off `$a0`):

```
lw   $at, off($a0)
nop ; nop ; nop
andi $at, $at, 0x100
nop
bnez $at, <self>
nop
jr   $ra
lui  $ra, 0x7000
```

They use `$at` as their working register and write `$ra` in the return's delay slot, which cc1 never emits. This is AGENTS.md's second "Handwritten assembly" criterion, which asks for a maintainer's agreement in review: please accept or reject the classification on its own. It is kept separate from my matching PR #337 for that reason. These rows are in my #152 reservation.
